title: Bioorthogonal Chemical Imaging of Cell Metabolism Regulated by Aromatic Amino Acids
protocol: Prepare 10 mL of control media in Dulbecco's modified Eagle medium (DMEM) containing 50% D2O.
Measure and mix 10 mg of DMEM powder with 4.7 mL of double distilled water (ddH2O).
Thoroughly vortex and invert the tube to ensure the solution is well mixed.
Add 4.7 mL of D2O, 0.5 mL of fetal bovine serum (FBS) at 5%, and 0.1 mL of penicillin/streptomycin (PS) at 1%.
Thoroughly vortex and invert the tube to ensure the solution is well mixed.
Prepare 10 mL of excess phenylalanine (Phe) treatment medium in DMEM containing 50% D2O.
Measure and mix 10 mg of DMEM powder with 4.7 mL of ddH2O, 0.5 mL of FBS at 5%, and 0.1 mL of PS at 1%.
Thoroughly vortex and invert the tube to ensure the solution is well mixed.
Add excess Phe powder at a concentration of 924 mg/L.
Thoroughly vortex and invert the tube to ensure the solution is well mixed.
Prepare 10 mL of excess tryptophan (Trp) treatment medium in DMEM containing 50% D2O.
Measure and mix 10 mg of DMEM powder with 4.7 mL of ddH2O, 0.5 mL of FBS at 5%, and 0.1 mL of PS at 1%.
Thoroughly vortex and invert the tube to ensure the solution is well mixed.
Add excess Trp powder at a concentration of 224 mg/L.
Thoroughly vortex and invert the tube to ensure the solution is well mixed.
Add methionine at 30.0 mg/mL to all conical tubes.
Add threonine at 95.0 mg/mL to all conical tubes.
Thoroughly vortex and invert the tube containing methionine and threonine.
Filter the control and treatment media with a 25 mm syringe filter featuring a 0.22 µm polyethersulfone membrane.
Seal all media-contained conical tubes with parafilm.
Store sealed conical tubes at 4 °C for up to 3 weeks.
Warm all media to 37°C prior to treating cells.
Maintain HeLa cells in culture flasks using standard DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Sub-culture HeLa cells at a split ratio of 1:10 until reaching 80% or higher cell viability.
Seed 2 x 10^5 HeLa cells per well onto a 24-well plate using DMEM supplemented with 0.5% FBS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin once confluency reaches 80% or higher.
Prepare a 24-well plate with sterilized, poly-d-lysin, laminin-coated round coverslips, 12 mm in diameter.
Submerge coverslips in 70% ethanol and dry gently using lint-free wipes.
Wash the cells once with 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) without magnesium and calcium ions.
Add 0.25% trypsin to dissociate adherent cells from the flask.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 3 min.
Add DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Gently pipette up and down.
Collect the cells by centrifugation at 300 x g at room temperature (RT) for 3 min.
Resuspend the cells in DMEM supplemented with 0.5% FBS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer, light microscope, and trypan blue.
Seed a density of 2 x 10^5 cells per well of a 24-well plate.
Return the cells to the incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Gently shake the plate to distribute the cells evenly.
Replace the old culture media with 50% D2O/excess Phe or 50% D2O/excess Tryp media after 8 h.
Return the cells to the incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 36 h.
Prepare microscope slides with imaging spacers 9 mm in diameter before fixing.
Place 15 μL of 1x PBS supplemented with calcium and magnesium ions on the slides.
Rinse the cells with 1x PBS supplemented with calcium and magnesium ions.
Add 0.5 mL of 4% methanol-free paraformaldehyde (PFA) solution.
Leave the plate under the biosafety hood for approximately 15 min.
Aspirate the PFA solution and rinse with 1x PBS supplemented with calcium and magnesium ions twice.
Add 1.5 mL of 1x PBS supplemented with calcium and magnesium ions in each well.
Gently grab the coverslips out of each well using sterile tweezers.
Invert and place the cell-containing side of the coverslips onto the imaging spacers to contact the PBS prepared in step 2.5.1.
Seal the outer layer of the coverslip with the imaging spacer using transparent nail polish.
Store the microscope slides at 4 °C when not imaging.
Turn on the laser by turning the key to the ON position.
Double-click on the LabSpec6 software icon to open the acquisition software.
Load the biological sample onto the sample holder directly underneath the objective lens.
Click the Camera icon in the software to turn on the video camera.
Adjust the focus plane to identify a region of interest with the 50x objective lens.
Move the joystick to control the planer translation of the XY stage and rotate the joystick to change the depth of focus.
Switch to the 100x objective lens with 40 mW of excitation power after choosing the position for measurement.
Click the red Stop icon in the software to turn off the video camera.
Select a grating of 1800 lines/mm, and set the acquisition range from 400 cm-1 to 3,150 cm-1.
Set the Acquisition Time to 90 s.
Set the Accumulation to 3.
Set the Binning to 4 for least noise and most accurate spectrum.
Click the Arrow icon to turn on real-time display.
Tune the Raman shift (cm-1) to 2,850 cm-1.
Adjust the focus plane with the joystick to optimize signal-to-noise ratio.
Click the red Stop icon for a real-time display.
Select the Circle icon to start spectrum acquisition.
Use the same focus plane to measure background with PBS.
Subtract the background spectrum from each subcellular target spectrum using software like Origin.
Press the main switch of the control box IX3-CBH to On.
Press the main switch of the touch panel controller to On.
Press the main switch of the AC adapter of the power supply for LD OBIS 6 Laser Remote connected to the main laser combiner FV31-SCOMB to On.
Press the main switch of the AC adapter of the power supply for LD OBIS 6 Laser Remote connected to the sub laser combiner FV31-SCOMB to On.
Press the main switches of the Si photodiode detector and lock-in amplifier On.
Set the Stokes Beam at 1,031 nm.
Set the Pulse Width at 6 ps.
Set the Repetition Rate at 80 MHz.
Couple into the microscope.
Set the picoEmerald system supplied with a synchronized pump beam with a Tunable Wavelength from 720-990 nm.
Set the Pulse Width of both the pump and Stokes beams to 5-6 ps.
Set the Repetition Rate of both the pump and Stokes beams to 80 MHz.
Adjust the average excitation power of both the pump and Stokes beams to 450 mW.
Optimize the excitation power to minimize photodamage for the sample.
Use a high-numerical aperture (NA) oil condenser with an NA of 1.4 to collect the Stokes and pump beams where the sample is mounted by emitting a few drops on the condenser.
Mount the sample on the oil.
Place a large water droplet on top of the microscope slide where the sample is fixed for the water-immersion objective lens.
Set the lock-in amplifier to 20 MHz.
Process the image using the super-resolution software module.
Select 512 pixels x 512 pixels and 80 µs/pixel for the dwell time.
Acquire the image once the desired cellular region is focused properly.
Save images as an Olympus .oir graphic file using the acquisition software of the microscope.
Acquire a background image at 1,900 cm-1.
Subtract the background image from all cellular images.
Set the label-free autofluorescence of Flavin to 800 nm and NADH to 780 nm for 2PEF imaging.
Use a 460 nm/515 nm filter cube to collect Flavin and NADH autofluorescence backscattered emission.
Adjust the dwell time to 8 µs/pixel and set the pixel size to 512 pixels x 512 pixels for 2PEF imaging.
Set the laser shutter power parameter to 150 mW for 2PEF imaging.
Tune the stimulated Raman loss to 2,850 cm-1 (797 nm) for 3D image reconstruction.
Register the laser to scan from the top focus plane to detect the top and bottom layers of single cells for 3D image reconstruction.
Generate and save 3D models as .oir files.
Convert the spectral files into an array.
Interpolate the spectra at every reciprocal centimeter.
Graph the raw data for validation.
Perform baseline correction on the raw spectra using the built-in function msbackadj in MATLAB.
Estimate baseline points at separation-unit values identified by users.
Draw a regression line from the estimated baseline points.
Smooth the regression line to subtract the baseline from each individual raw spectrum.
Normalize the Raman intensity of the protein at 2,930 cm-1 by dividing it with the intensity of each Raman shift.
Average the individual spectra of the same condition into a single spectrum to reduce noise.
Use applications such as Origin to display all the spectra simultaneously.
Process all 3D images using FIJI-ImageJ software.
Perform bandpass filters for the 3D image stacks.
Smooth the 3D image stacks.
For 3D image analysis, assign each lipid droplet to a spherical score by measuring the distance between its center of mass and surface.
Compare each spherical score with a spherical score of a perfect sphere on the same Euclidean plan.
Discard lipid droplets with low spherical scores.
Evaluate the volume and counts of remaining lipid droplets.
Analyze the volume and counts of lipid droplets between different treatments for statistical significance using GraphPad Prism.
Use FIJI-ImageJ software to process all 2D hyperspectral images.
Select the 2,930 cm-1 channel to make a mask image containing 0 and 1 values.
Assign background to 0 and cellular region to 1 in the mask image.
Subtract the deuterium-labeled protein channel (2,175 cm-1) from the background channel (1,900 cm-1) to remove fluorescent effects.
Divide the resulting deuterium-labeled protein channel by the protein channel (2,930 cm-1) to obtain ratiometric images of protein turnover rates.
Multiply the mask image made in step 5.3.2 by the ratiometric images to remove background noise.
Use the Freehand Selection tool in FIJI-ImageJ to manually segment and calculate pixel intensities displayed on single cells.
The pixel intensities correspond to concentrations of chemical bonds being visualized.
Analyze the pixel intensities for statistical significance using a statistical software application.
Repeat the analysis with the remaining ratiometric data.
